problem: Are the nim-sequences of all finite octal games eventually periodic?
missing_details: Definition of a finite octal game (an octal code with only finitely many non-zero digits)
Definition of the nim-sequence as the sequence of Sprague–Grundy values G(n) for heap sizes n
Precise meaning of “eventually periodic” (existence of period p>0 and preperiod N₀ with G(n+p)=G(n) for all n≥N₀)
Assumption of normal-play convention for the Sprague–Grundy theorem
refined_question: Let an octal game be specified by an octal code 0.d₁d₂⋯ in which only finitely many digits dₖ are non-zero (a finite octal game). For each heap size n≥0 under normal-play conventions, let G(n) denote the Sprague–Grundy value (nim-value) of a single heap of size n. Does there exist, for every finite octal game, a positive integer period p and a non-negative integer preperiod N₀ such that for all n≥N₀, G(n+p)=G(n)?
justification: The original name identifies the three core objects—nim-sequences, finite octal games, and eventual periodicity—but omits their formal definitions and the precise periodicity condition. The refined question introduces definitions of finite octal games, the Sprague–Grundy nim-sequence, and the exact eventual periodicity requirement, matching the canonical open question as stated in the literature.
